What your address is used for

The pool sends some requests out through your address instead of the operator's. That spread is the whole point: if one address gets marked by the far end, the others keep working.

This is your address doing the job a Tor exit normally would — one egress among many, rotating by request rather than fixed. Your address is not a Tor node and is not announced as one; it is simply one of several exits the pool can pick, so a mark against one does not fall on all.

These switches are remembered in this browser and nothing else happens: there is no hub to tell about them. The page is honest about that rather than pretending the offer is live.

What a user cannot do

  • Add tokens or sessions — that is the partner role
  • Raise the account-pool allowance
  • See other people in the pool
  • Change features or clear sessions

If you have accounts to contribute, sign in as a partner on the sign-in page — that role gets its own page.
